findings.finding: The hosted ledger is not an admissible baseline for either existing successor. The 86->97 controller requires targetCount=0 and priorCount=86 at rehearsal start; the already-recorded evidence migrations or any partially installed predecessor row make that exact stage-0 state impossible.

The 97->102 feature successor cannot follow the hosted topology unchanged. If the three evidence rows are retained while all eleven predecessor rows are installed, its non-feature prefix becomes 100 instead of 97. Its preflight therefore fails closed even though the five feature rows are currently absent.

Q1 and Q3 resolve the expected-version topology and the 86-row identity mapping. The retained October 4 snapshot matches 62 rows exactly; canonical parsing matches 23 of the 24 later rows to current sources or immutable applied receipts; the remaining hosted row is an identified historical applied variant that must be preserved as observed.

The evidence migrations are observed before their intended 102->105 promotion. Existing 102 evidence must not be relabeled as hosted 105 evidence, and the current manifests must remain pinned to their original transitions.

The isolated PG17.6 evidence-first constituent replay validated 12 predecessor and 6 feature stages through ledger 105. A separate fresh-container replay then executed the compiler-produced 11-plan and 5-plan aggregate SQL strings in one outer transaction per phase and matched their terminal state identities. Both proofs preserved the source dump hash and removed all disposable containers; operating admission remains held.

The c975c881... value came from 86 synthetic local_predecessor fixture rows inserted by the historical PG17 harness after verifying its application ledger was empty. Its difference from the hosted f2791773... raw-statement root is expected and is not hosted drift. A new contract must keep rehearsal-fixture identity and operating baseline identity separate.

Hosted row 20261008124858/public_profile_leaderboard_read_boundary is pinned as an immutable operating predecessor identity. The new contracts reject substitution by current source 20261008084856, while launch remains held until a fresh operating readback confirms that identity.

recommendedReadOnlyQueries.purpose: Return at most 19 expected ledger rows with names and statement-vector hashes; no statement bodies or user data are returned.
recommendedReadOnlyQueries.observedResult: Only the three evidence rows were present, and all three identities matched.

recommendedReadOnlyQueries.purpose: Hash the remaining ledger after excluding the three observed evidence versions using the controller's material expression.
recommendedReadOnlyQueries.sql: SELECT pg_catalog.jsonb_build_object('count', pg_catalog.count(*), 'root', pg_catalog.encode(pg_catalog.sha256(pg_catalog.convert_to(COALESCE(pg_catalog.jsonb_agg(pg_catalog.jsonb_build_object('version', version, 'name', name, 'statements', statements) ORDER BY version), '[]'::jsonb)::text, 'UTF8')), 'hex')) FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations WHERE version <> ALL (ARRAY['20261017043000','20261017140000','20261017160000']::text[]);

recommendedReadOnlyQueries.purpose: Return at most 87 non-evidence ledger identities so the 86-row root mismatch can be localized without returning statement bodies or user data.
recommendedReadOnlyQueries.observedResult: All 86 bounded row identities were retained in hosted-ledger-mapping-20261018.json and classified locally.
recommendedReadOnlyQueries.sql: WITH bounded AS (SELECT version, name, pg_catalog.cardinality(statements)::int AS statement_count, pg_catalog.encode(pg_catalog.sha256(pg_catalog.convert_to(pg_catalog.array_to_json(statements)::text, 'UTF8')), 'hex') AS statement_vector_sha256 FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations WHERE version <> ALL (ARRAY['20261017043000','20261017140000','20261017160000']::text[]) ORDER BY version, name LIMIT 87) SELECT pg_catalog.jsonb_build_object('count', pg_catalog.count(*), 'rows', COALESCE(pg_catalog.jsonb_agg(pg_catalog.jsonb_build_object('version', version, 'name', name, 'statement_count', statement_count, 'statement_vector_sha256', statement_vector_sha256) ORDER BY version, name), '[]'::jsonb)) FROM bounded;
